headline: UniTask is an open-source student manager built with AI
summary: This new app helps students manage timetables, deadlines, and to-dos, with offline backups and group sharing features.
details: A developer has created UniTask, an open-source university task manager app designed to help students organize their academic lives. The app was built using Google AI Studio and Claude, leveraging AI to streamline the development process.

UniTask offers a range of features including daily lecture schedule management with start alerts, assignment deadline tracking with persistent alarms, and personal recurring to-do lists. It also supports offline JSON backups for data security.

For collaborative learning, UniTask allows users to join study groups by sharing a simple code, enabling them to share tasks and stay coordinated with classmates. The developer is actively seeking feedback and suggestions for future improvements.

The app's interface displays a weekly lecture schedule, showing course names, timings, locations, and instructors. It also highlights pending assignments, providing a clear overview of academic responsibilities.

headline_marked: Reddit [[introduces 'For You' feed]] to compete with TikTok
headline: Reddit introduces 'For You' feed to compete with TikTok
summary: The platform is rolling out a new feed experience that combines followed communities with algorithmically-driven recommendations, aiming to boost discovery and engagement.
details: Reddit is the latest social platform to adopt the “For You” feed popularized by TikTok. Users will now see two options when opening the platform: “For You” and “Following.”

The “For You” feed combines posts from communities users have joined with recommendations tailored to their interests. Reddit says the feature will help users discover relevant communities and conversations they might not have otherwise come across.
The “Following” feed only displays posts from communities they have joined. Reddit says the change is designed to foster connection, participation, and belonging.

Reddit is likely hoping that the redesigned feed experience will nudge users to engage with content beyond the communities they already follow. It also brings Reddit more in line with the recommendation-driven experience that’s become standard across social media.
With the launch, Reddit joins a number of popular platforms that have adopted “For You”-style feeds, including Instagram, X, Threads, and Facebook.

Some users who encountered the new feed during its initial testing phase have already expressed frustration with the change, preferring the more focused feed experience of only seeing posts from communities they’ve joined.
Reddit says users can switch between feeds and return to the one they last viewed the next time they open the platform.
The new feed experience is rolling out globally over the next few weeks.
